item.title: Downloads surge for Meta's new AI agent Muse
item.description: Meta's new AI personal assistant, Muse, has reached the top of the U.S. App Store charts, surpassing competitor ChatGPT. CBS News digital reporter Lauren Fichten details how the app's popularity is helping Meta play catch-up in the AI race.

item.title: Grand jury declines to indict anyone in death of Nolan Wells
item.description: Nolan Wells, 18, was found dead after going missing following an outing with friends on Mississippi's Horn Island on the Fourth of July.

item.title: U.S. Mint and America's VetDogs unveil commemorative coins honoring service dogs
item.description: In honor of September as National Service Dog Month, the U.S. Mint and the nonprofit America's VetDogs unveiled the final designs for three commemorative coins recognizing the impact service animals have on those living with disabilities. America's VetDogs President and CEO John Miller, along with Navy veteran and Paralympic gold medalist Max Rohn, join with more.

item.title: Trump tells U.N. General Assembly he will either strike a deal with Iran or "annihilate" country
item.description: President Trump spoke about the Iran war in his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, telling diplomats that he might choose to "annihilate" the country. CBS News' Natalie Brand breaks it down.

item.title: Georgia couple who survived Nepal flood shares their story
item.description: Mita and Hemant Parikh decided to split from their group and take a side trip during their long-planned pilgrimage. They're now safely back home, but none of the families they were traveling with have been found.

item.title: Hurricane Polo grows into powerful Category 5 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensified in the Pacific off the southwestern Mexican coast, growing into a Category 5 storm. Here's the latest on its path.

item.title: AOC says she'll decide on presidential run after midterms
item.description: In an interview with The New York Times, Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez discussed the possibility of running for president in 2028. Former Republican Rep. Patrick McHenry of North Carolina and Democratic strategist Corbin Trent join with analysis.

item.title: State of key races with 6 weeks until midterms
item.description: Tuesday marks six weeks until Election Day. CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto and Sabato's Crystal Ball managing editor Kyle Kondik join to unpack the latest numbers.

item.title: Rep. Analilia Mejia calls ICE a "rogue agency" that needs to be abolished
item.description: Democratic Rep. Analilia Mejia of New Jersey joins "The Takeout" to discuss last weekend's ICE shooting of a man in Austin, Texas, and the push for a pause on new data centers in her state.

item.title: Trump rejects calls to rein in AI: "We're gonna encourage it"
item.description: At the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday, President Trump told world leaders that the U.S. rejects efforts to rein in artificial intelligence. Stephen Witt, a journalist focused on AI, joins "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: Meta's Muse shopping agent is a hit, as AI commerce starts to take off
item.description: Meta's new AI tool now ranks at the top of the App Store. Some retail experts see a "natural evolution from search."

item.title: What to know about Trump's U.N. address and his annihilation threat for Iran
item.description: President Trump threatened to "annihilate" Iran and defended his handling of world conflicts in his U.N. speech on Tuesday. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe reports. Then, Foreign Policy editor-in-chief Ravi Agrawal joins with analysis.

item.title: ICE officer who shot Venezuelan man wasn't wearing body camera, sources say
item.description: The ICE officer who shot a Venezuelan delivery driver was not wearing a body camera at the time of the shooting, sources familiar with the investigation told CBS News.

item.title: Man shot by ICE being detained with bullet still in his back, lawyer says
item.description: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, the 28-year-old Venezuelan national shot by an ICE officer on Sunday, said in a phone call on Monday that he's "not doing well."

item.title: Andreessen Horowitz launches AI school as college alternative
item.description: One of Silicon Valley's most prominent venture investors is gearing its new tech academy toward aspiring entrepreneurs focused on building AI.

item.title: Inside the significance of Kamala Harris campaigning with Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Former Vice President Kamala Harris is campaigning for Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. CBS News White House reporter Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: 2 Republican Senate candidates call for swift end to Iran war with midterms approaching
item.description: As the 2026 midterm elections get closer, more Republicans are speaking out against the war in Iran. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose, coroner says
item.description: A South Carolina coroner revealed Tuesday that actor Hayden Panettiere died from an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl. CBS News national correspondent Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Trump says he's deciding between deal or driving Iran "into hell"
item.description: President Trump tells the U.N. he has a "big decision to make" on whether to make a deal or drive Iran "into hell."

item.title: What is the White House press pool and how does it work?
item.description: President Trump's move to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House has highlighted the role of the press pool.

item.title: Trump to U.N.: Whoever wins AI, wins
item.description: President Trump continued his push for rapid AI development Tuesday in remarks before the United Nations General Assembly. Global affairs analyst Jonathan Wachtel joined CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump signs agreement giving U.S. broad military authority in Greenland
item.description: The U.S., Denmark and Greenland signed a new security agreement bolstering the United States' military and security presence on the island.

item.title: In U.N. speech, Trump threatens to "annihilate" Iran and defends foreign policy
item.description: President Trump said he could "annihilate" Iran while predicting that Tehran would make a deal to end the war after the U.S. midterm elections.

item.title: Senators press Rubio to prioritize release of American held in Iran
item.description: Reza Valizadeh, a U.S.-Iranian dual citizen and former journalist for U.S.-funded broadcaster Radio Farda, has been imprisoned in Iran since September 2024.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose, autopsy finds
item.description: An autopsy by the Greenville County Coroner's Office determined Hayden Panettiere's death was due to an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl.

item.title: What is an "AI swarm," and why is it giving tech experts nightmares?
item.description: AI "agents" show a remarkable ability to share information and knowledge with other bots. That should worry us.

item.title: Flights resume at NYC-area airports following equipment outage, FAA says
item.description: Flights at Newark Liberty International, John F. Kennedy International and LaGuardia airports were delayed due to an equipment outage, the FAA says.

item.title: Man shot by ICE in custody with bullet lodged near his spine, lawyer says
item.description: In Austin, Texas, an ICE officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old Venezuelan man who, according to his lawyer, is now in federal custody with a bullet lodged in his spine. Jason Allen has video from the scene and more details.

item.title: Patrick Clancy says he still talks to his kids "all the time"
item.description: This Sunday on 60 Minutes, Patrick Clancy talks about his grief, his memories of his children, and the baseless conspiracy theories that flooded social media since his ex-wife's murder trial.

item.title: Scores killed, Americans among hundreds missing after Nepal, Tibet flash floods
item.description: The flash floods decimated villages, slamming into houses, roads, bridges and power plants.
